justifications.c1: Testing spend is the main cost: ~£1,000/yr for a six-flat block (Safelincs leaseholder post, search-confirmed), £50.99/visit (low-credibility pages.dev contractor site with self-conflicting prices), Whitecroft '£3,000/yr' (vendor); fines exist (Morecambe £4,500 for unmaintained emergency lighting, £22.5k total, search-confirmed), but annual saving per small block (~£600–1,200) is unlikely to reach 5x TCO of relay plus per-fitting tags.
justifications.c2: Monthly functional test mandated per BS 5266/BS EN 50172 (FPA, forum, LBBD monthly test document, Longhurst policy), so 1–3 tests in a pilot; not weekly or daily.
justifications.c3: Paid monthly contracts are documented and quantified (PA Housing monthly service contract, £1,000/yr forum post, £50.99/visit), but the file also shows a caretaker with a fish key can test without qualification, weakening the 'contractor visit is unavoidable' premise.
justifications.c4: FSO 2005 Art 17 maintenance duty, BS 5266 in common parts (TPI, GOV.UK purpose-built flats guide), and enforcement in residential premises: Morecambe prosecution specifically for emergency-lighting maintenance (search-confirmed), LFB enforcement notices, Bedford £40k (office), Lincolnshire FOI on emergency-lighting enforcement.
justifications.c5: Responsible Person is the freeholder, managing agent or housing association, and testing is a monthly service-charge line (PA Housing), but no job title or budget holder is evidenced and cost is passed through to leaseholders.
justifications.c6: Fire/electrical contractors already visit monthly, and the FIA promotes LuxIntelligent retrofit automated-testing savings to its members, showing the channel sells adjacent automated testing.
justifications.c7: Cheap good-enough substitute: self-test fittings cost about £8 more than standard (Lyco £36.99 vs £28.99; SparksDirect £15 ex VAT), plus LuxIntelligent, Hochiki Nepto, EMC and mobile-managed testing; no subscription prices and the retrofit gap is inference.
justifications.c8: Fish-key test circuits give an attach point, but a relay on a fixed lighting circuit is electrician work under BS 7671, a photodiode tag is needed on every fitting, and no component prices were searched.
justifications.c9: Monthly testing and a logbook recur for the building's life (logbook duty sourced only to a low-credibility pages.dev guide), and landlords pay monthly contracts, but no comparable subscription price exists (Hochiki's cloud service only 'in development').
justifications.c10: Leaseholder forum complaint about cost (Safelincs), enforcement cases and notices (Morecambe, Bedford, LFB, Lincolnshire FOI), and trade press (FPA, Landlord Today, FIA); several items are title-only and the first-hand pain is a single post.

weakest: Cheap substitutes: £8-premium self-test fittings plus an unqualified caretaker with a fish key already meet the monthly test, so a relay-plus-per-fitting-tag retrofit saves at most ~£600–1,200 a year per small block.
